lastCommit.message:
[ota-hal] OTA-1716 — every row in "what moved it" says what it is

Your notation: *"in the 'what moved it' section of the expanded character screen,
everything listed in it should be able to be tapped on to see what it is. as of
now, only wrongs and gifts do."*

⚠⚠⚠ WHY THOSE TWO AND NOTHING ELSE — which is the part worth fixing rather than
patching. Neither of them was tappable because anyone decided that row deserved a
drill-down. They were tappable because each happened to own a LEDGER — the gifts
arrays for one, the wrongs ledger for the other — and each got its own useState
boolean and its own branch in the renderer at the moment you tapped it and found
it flat. OTA-1161 was the first; OTA-1683 was you reporting the second. Under
that shape, making a row tappable is a bespoke job, so it only ever happened in
response to a notation. Fourteen kinds of row, two of them answering.

⚠⚠ SO THE FIX IS WHERE THE NUMBER IS MADE, not in the screen. `regardParts` now
returns a `detail` alongside every value it pushes, written in the same branch,
from the same variables — the corruption row's explanation is composed inside the
`if` that reads corruption, using corruption. A help screen written separately
from the arithmetic is a second copy of the rules, and this project has paid for
copied thresholds three times (OTA-1156, OTA-1158, OTA-1448). The screen drops
its two booleans for one open-set keyed by row index, so a row is tappable
because it exists, and all three render paths go through the same toggle.

⚠ AND THE DETAILS EARN THE TAP. A drill-down that restates the row is the tap you
already had, so:

  · "someone down here vouches for you" names the faction and its standing. That
    word "someone" is exactly what the row could not previously cash.
  · "your answer: Sell the letters on  −5" opens into the QUESTION he asked, the
    hint that option carried, and the sentence it bought on your ending screen.
    That row is the heaviest single input in the whole score and the one most
    unreadable months later, which is why OTA-1085 itemised it in the first place.
  · "N debts made good" names who each one was cleared with.
  · Corruption and menace show the raw number, where the count starts, and the
    floor. Lore, relics kept and relics sold show the count and the cap, so you
    can see when a dial has saturated and stop feeding it.
  · The pressure row names your difficulty tier outright.

The two ledger rows keep their ledgers — they read live data the score does not
hold, and duplicating them into `detail` would have been the second copy this
whole change is about avoiding.

⚠ TWO INSTRUMENTS. One drives a character who has done one of everything and
asserts no row comes back flat. The other reads the source and requires each of
the 14 push sites to carry a ledger kind or a detail, so row fifteen fails the
build even if no fixture reaches it. That second one caught my own first attempt:
a line-shaped regex silently skipped the three rows written on one line, which
would have left the instrument agreeing with itself while measuring two thirds of
the file.

A row that somehow reaches the screen with nothing to add still opens and says
so. Silence on tap is the defect.
